solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Dessert wine’s disturbing repercussion (10)

blocks.note: afters = pudding, the course after the main one
hock = a German white wine

annotation.surface: A pudding wine that leaves an unpleasant aftermath, perhaps a hangover.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Afters' is British slang for dessert, and hock is a British name for Rhine wine. The 's reads as 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Literally a tremor after an earthquake, and by extension any unsettling consequence that follows an event.

entries.clue: Juliet in sober group with kiss for hero (4)

indicatorNotes.in: 'Juliet in sober group' puts J physically inside the group's letters
indicatorNotes.with: 'with kiss' means accompanied by it, so the kiss is tacked on at the end

blocks.note: Alcoholics Anonymous, whose members stay sober
J in the NATO alphabet; it goes inside AA
X = a kiss at the end of a letter

annotation.surface: A romantic hero finds Juliet at a temperance meeting and kisses her.
annotation.walkthrough: The Juliet and kiss suggest Romeo, but the hero is the Greek warrior of the Trojan War.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Greek warrior of the Trojan War, second only to Achilles in Homer.

entries.clue: Rapid work from man in worn coat (7)

indicatorNotes.in: the man is dressed in the coat, so he goes inside its letters
indicatorNotes.worn: a worn coat has lost its shape, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram of COAT; split TOC…A
cat = a man, in jazz slang; it goes between TOC and A

annotation.surface: A tailor dashes off a job for a man whose coat is threadbare.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Work' is a musical work, not a job of mending.
annotation.definitionFit: A musical term: a fast, showy keyboard piece, a 'work' in the composer's sense.

entries.clue: Crazed dance after drinks (5,3,5)

indicatorNotes.after: 'dance after drinks' puts the dance later, so it follows the drinks in the answer

blocks.note: a round = drinks bought for the whole group
the twist = the 1960s dance

annotation.surface: Wild dancing once everyone has had a few drinks.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a party getting out of hand, which makes 'Crazed' look like a description of the dancers.
annotation.definitionFit: A British idiom for mad, as in 'you're driving me round the twist'.

entries.clue: Disheartened Greek woman (6)

indicatorNotes.Disheartened: the heart of a word is its middle, so a disheartened word loses its central letter

blocks.note: a Hellene is a Greek; its central L is removed

annotation.surface: A Greek woman who has lost heart.
annotation.walkthrough: HELLENE has seven letters, so its heart is the fourth, one of the two Ls.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Hélène is a French woman's name.

entries.clue: Horse-drawn transport and saddle for romantic writer (8)

blocks.note: a cart is pulled by a horse
to saddle someone with a job = to land them with it

annotation.surface: A horse and saddle for a writer of romantic novels, all galloping heroes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Saddle' looks like horse gear beside the cart, but it is the verb: to burden.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Barbara Cartland, the prolific British author of romance novels.

entries.clue: Characters regularly appearing in Shanghai Story (4)

indicatorNotes.Characters regularly appearing in: characters are letters, and regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

annotation.surface: Actors who turn up regularly in a drama set in Shanghai.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Characters' sounds like people in a story, but here it means letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a saga is a long story, originally a Norse one.

entries.clue: Song about endless division in state (7)

indicatorNotes.about: 'about' means around, so the song goes around the division
indicatorNotes.endless: without an end, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: an aria is an operatic song; split ARI…A
ZONE, a division, without its E

annotation.surface: A song about partition in a divided country.
annotation.walkthrough: 'State' looks political, alongside division, but it is a US state.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Arizona is one of the fifty US states.

entries.clue: Improve American energy after raising oil price (10)

indicatorNotes.raising: in a down clue, raising a word lifts it so it reads bottom to top

blocks.note: Am. = American
E = energy in physics
OIL written upwards
a rate = a price charged

annotation.surface: America's energy situation improves after the oil price rises.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Raising oil price' reads as one economic phrase, but 'raising' applies to oil alone.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to ameliorate is to make a bad situation better.

entries.clue: Report of a barbarous gathering (7)

indicatorNotes.Report of: a report is something heard, so the answer is how the words sound

blocks.note: barbarous = cruel

annotation.surface: A news report of a savage mob.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gathering' looks like the crowd in the surface, but it is a gradual accumulation.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in its financial sense: interest or debt building up over time is gathering.

entries.clue: Get to mislead with Republican replacing Democrat (7)

indicatorNotes.replacing: one thing replacing another takes its place, so R goes where D was

blocks.note: to deceive = to mislead
R for Republican takes the place of D for Democrat

annotation.surface: A US politician wins over voters by switching party.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Get to' looks like a phrase ('manage to'), but 'Get' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to get a letter is to receive it.

entries.clue: Copper on wagon tried drinking new wine to meet expectations (3,3,7)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, a word on another sits above it, so copper comes first
indicatorNotes.drinking: something drinking takes the drink inside it, so tried surrounds the wine

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
on the wagon = teetotal, TT
a court heard (tried) the case; split HE…ARD
must = grape juice before fermenting

annotation.surface: A policeman on the wagon tried some new wine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Copper' is a policeman in the surface but a chemical element here. 'On wagon' yields TT because someone on the wagon is teetotal.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: something that cuts the mustard is up to standard.

entries.clue: Doctor left a grand residence (6,4)

indicatorNotes.Doctor: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

annotation.surface: A doctor bequeathed a thousand pounds and a large house.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a person leaving money in a will, but it is the verb. 'Grand' is £1000 in the surface, only letters here.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a garden flat is a ground-floor home opening onto a garden.

entries.clue: Some kimono binder? (3)

indicatorNotes.Some: 'some' of a phrase is only part of it, so the answer sits inside the words

blocks.note: the last letter of this word
the opening two letters of this word

annotation.surface: A question about what ties a kimono.
annotation.walkthrough: The words holding the answer also define it, so the whole clue does both jobs at once.
annotation.definitionFit: The whole clue reads straight: the obi is the broad sash that binds a kimono.

entries.clue: No X in Mr RM Nixon? There’s one! (10)

annotation.definition: No X in Mr RM Nixon? There’s one!

blocks.clueFragment: No X in Mr RM Nixon?
blocks.note: read as a quip about the president's name, and meant as a string of letters to be read in both directions
read as pointing out an X, and meant as pointing at the whole phrase as an example of a word-game curiosity

annotation.surface: A remark that Richard Nixon's name has no X, as if it were a word game.
annotation.walkthrough: Read 'No X in Mr RM Nixon' backwards letter by letter: it is identical both ways.
annotation.definitionFit: The clue gives an example of the thing itself: a phrase that reads the same backwards as forwards.

entries.clue: Helicopter swiftly circling hospital (6)

indicatorNotes.circling: to circle something is to go round it, so swiftly surrounds hospital

blocks.note: apace = quickly; split APAC…E
H = hospital, as on road signs

annotation.surface: An air ambulance circles a hospital at speed.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a rescue helicopter; the answer is a gunship.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Apache is a US Army attack helicopter.

entries.clue: Article put out on home brewing (2,3,3)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, one thing on another comes after it, so these pieces follow home

blocks.note: at home = in
the definite article
to air = to broadcast, put out

annotation.surface: A magazine piece published about making beer at home.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Brewing' suggests beer, next to home, but here it means about to happen, as trouble brews.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: change that is in the air is imminent, just as a storm is brewing.

entries.clue: Deviate from course over Channel in Eurofighter? (8)

indicatorNotes.over: in a down clue, a word over another sits above it, so WARP comes first

blocks.note: to warp = to bend out of true
a lane = a channel, as a shipping lane

annotation.surface: A jet strays off course over the English Channel.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital C makes 'Channel' look like the English Channel; it is only a lane. The question mark flags the Eurofighter as one example.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Eurofighter Typhoon is a European combat jet.

entries.clue: Granite mixed with sulphur: it won’t react (5,3)

indicatorNotes.mixed with: things mixed together lose their order, so granite and S are stirred into new letters

blocks.note: anagram fodder
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

annotation.surface: A chemistry note: granite mixed with sulphur is unreactive.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface stays in the chemistry lab throughout, which hides the anagram well.
annotation.definitionFit: A description rather than a synonym: gases like neon and argon are called inert because they barely react.

entries.clue: Pass comment where animals were once held? (7)

blocks.note: ex = former, once
a pound is an enclosure where stray animals are kept
completes the pound phrase, split by 'once'; no letters of its own

annotation.surface: Remarks about an old animal enclosure.
annotation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads as one phrase: a former pound. 'Once' is wedged inside it.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: to expound is to set out views on a subject, passing comment at length.

entries.clue: Surrounded by 500 in a film (6)

indicatorNotes.in: '500 in a film' puts the 500 inside, so D goes within the other letters

blocks.note: a mist = a film, as of condensation; split AMI…ST
D = 500 in Roman numerals

annotation.surface: A cast of 500 extras in a film.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Film' looks like a movie, but it is a thin layer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to be amidst things is to be among them, surrounded by them.

entries.clue: Seabird for example about to take different direction (7)

indicatorNotes.about: 'about' as in 'about turn', so EG is turned round

blocks.note: a diver = a loon, a diving seabird
e.g. = for example

annotation.surface: A seabird about to change course.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'on the point of', but 'about' belongs to the example and 'to' is only a link.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: roads that diverge split and head different ways.

entries.clue: For something sweet, come together at Oval? (6)

blocks.note: a team gels when it comes together
used as printed
the letter O is oval in shape

annotation.surface: Something sweet for a gathering at the Oval.
annotation.walkthrough: The Oval is a London cricket ground, which the surface uses; the wordplay only wants its shape.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: gelato is Italian ice cream, one kind of something sweet.

entries.clue: Pickpocket departs with as little money as possible (3)

blocks.note: d. = departs, in timetables
1p, one penny, the smallest coin

annotation.surface: A pickpocket runs off with barely any money.
annotation.walkthrough: The smallest British coin is the penny, 1p, whose digit 1 stands for I.
annotation.definitionFit: A slang sense: a dip dips a hand into other people's pockets.

entries.clue: Magnificent: the writer’s gift-wrapped volume? (10)

indicatorNotes.wrapped: a wrapped present has paper all round it, so the gift surrounds the volume

blocks.note: the writer is = I'm
pressie = a present; split PRESSI…E
v = volume

annotation.surface: A writer boasts of a splendid book wrapped as a present.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The writer' is the setter, so 'the writer's' becomes I'M. 'Pressie' is British slang for a present.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something magnificent makes a strong impression.

entries.clue: Salacious material has stomachs turning (4)

indicatorNotes.turning: a word turning round faces the other way, so it reads backwards

blocks.note: tums = tummies, stomachs

annotation.surface: Filthy material that turns people's stomachs.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is exactly what such material does to a reader, which disguises the reversal.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: smut is indecent writing or pictures, material that is salacious.

entries.clue: One cracking old joke cheers prickly sort (7)

indicatorNotes.cracking: something cracking a shell breaks into it, so I goes inside the cheers

blocks.note: O = old
a pun is a joke
ta = thanks, cheers; split T…A
I = one, inside TA

annotation.surface: Someone cracking an old joke cheers up a grumpy person.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Prickly sort' looks like a grumpy person, but it is a cactus. 'Ta' and 'cheers' are both British for thanks.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the prickly pear cactus is a sort of plant covered in spines.

entries.clue: One from Plotinus might be unspoilt (7)

annotation.definition: One from Plotinus might be unspoilt

blocks.note: read as a saying of the Greek philosopher, and meant as a rearrangement of the letters of his name
read as praise for his thought, and meant as the actual word those eight letters make

annotation.surface: Something the philosopher Plotinus wrote might be pristine.
annotation.walkthrough: PLOTINUS and UNSPOILT use the same eight letters, so the clue names its own trick.
annotation.definitionFit: The clue describes the thing itself: a word made by rearranging another's letters.

entries.clue: What will increase circulation, rather like a senior journalist? (4)

blocks.note: read as boosting newspaper sales, and meant as water swirling round and round
an ed is an editor; add -y, as fishy is like a fish

annotation.surface: A question about what boosts a newspaper's circulation, like an editor.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Circulation' points at newspaper sales, which is the misdirection; the second sense is a made-up word.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses: water swirling in an eddy circulates, and 'eddy' is a jokey adjective for editor-like.

entries.clue: Support prior to defeat somewhat inferior (6-4)

indicatorNotes.prior to: prior to means before, so support comes first and defeat follows

blocks.note: to second a motion is to support it
to best someone = to defeat them

annotation.surface: Backing a side before it loses leaves you feeling rather inferior.
annotation.walkthrough: Both pieces are verbs, which the adjective definition conceals.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: what is second-best falls just short of the top, somewhat inferior.
